raw_response:
The bug is that txn_date is derived from ingest_ts instead of txn_ts. The 2026-01-16 refactor (DE-398) most likely introduced this. Every POSTED row (4582) has an ingest_ts one day after its txn_ts date, which matches the alert count exactly.

The fix is to derive txn_date from txn_ts. The evidence supports this: the monitor defines consistency as txn_date equal to the date of txn_ts, and the sample rows show txn_ts dates one day before ingest. Dropping the filter on status is not needed. Only the silver step needs replacing, because the gold tables are rebuilt from it.

Every other column keeps its meaning. Two checks:
- txn_id is distinct, so there are no duplicates to handle.
- The JOINs to customers and merchants are one-to-one, since both keys are unique.


{"diagnosis": "silver_transactions derives txn_date from CAST(ingest_ts AS DATE) instead of txn_ts (DE-398 refactor), so all 4582 POSTED rows get the next day's date. Deriving txn_date from txn_ts fixes silver and the downstream gold tables.", "decision": "fix", "confidence": 0.93, "pre_sql": [], "step_overrides": {"silver_transactions": "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE silver_transactions AS SELECT CAST(txn_id AS BIGINT) AS txn_id, customer_id, CAST(merchant_id AS INTEGER) AS merchant_id, CAST(amount AS DECIMAL(12,2)) AS amount, CAST(txn_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS txn_ts, CAST(txn_ts AS DATE) AS txn_date FROM raw_transactions WHERE status = 'POSTED'"}}
